Failed a Government Exam? How to Turn Failure into Success

2 min readBeginnerPunjab Police Sub Inspectorfailureexam motivationmindsetpunjab police si
Quick answer

Failures are part of success. I missed the Punjab Police SI cut-off by 10 marks before scoring 713 the next time. How to stop fearing failure and keep going.

≈ 2 min to finish · Beginner

When you start your study journey, you will face many failures along the way. Accept this from the start: there is no example of anyone succeeding without failing. Every person you call successful has failed at some point.

Failure is part of success

Failures are part of success. You move towards success by failing. So never fear failure, and never run from it.

My own failure

In my first Sub Inspector exam, I scored 613 and the cut-off was 623. I missed by just 10 marks. But I did not give up my preparation, and the next time I scored 713. If I had quit out of fear after that failure, those 100 marks would never have come. The full story is in my blog From 613 to 713.

My mantra: fight the battle, don't worry about the result

While studying, I always repeated one line: "Yudh karo, phal ki chinta mat karo" (fight the battle; don't worry about the result).

My only job was to fight, which meant to study. Whether I got the job or not, I did not worry about it. Worry only troubles you and pulls your focus away from studying. If you truly want the job, drop the worry and just do your work.

What to do after a failure

  • Accept it. It is part of the journey, not the end.
  • See where you lost marks and what to do differently next time. For me, it was previous year papers.
  • Keep preparing. One exam does not decide your future.
  • Stop worrying about the result and focus on the work.

You will reach success through failure.

Straight answers

Frequently asked questions

What should I do after failing a government exam?

Take a short break, find exactly where you lost marks, and fix that one thing. After missing the SI cut-off by 10 marks, I found my gap was previous year papers and scored 713 next time.

How do I stop fearing failure during preparation?

Focus on your work, not on the result. My mantra was "fight the battle, don't worry about the result": my only job was to study properly every day.
